newsitem.title: UK: Aframax tanker rates rise in north on lack of ship.
newsitem.headline: Aframax tanker rates rise in north on lack of ship.

text.p: The Aframax tanker market showed a firmer tone on Wednesday on a lack of tonnage in northern Europe and on bullish expectations in the Med, brokers said.
The last done rate in the inter-U.K./cont 80,000 tonne market was a heady W132.5, up from about W107.5 on Tuesday and under W90 last week, they added.
"The reason is quite simple -- a shortage of tonnage to the end of the month," a Scandinavian broker said.
Rates in the Med have not yet risen markedly but brokers said they were hopeful that they were about to rise.

Owners in the Med had been asking for as high as W165 for one particular cargo, and although they did not expect this level to be achieved, there was little doubt that the market was on its way up, they added.
"If owners get it right they will be able to push rates up," one broker said.
He said the market could firm to about W130/135 over the next few days from the current W117.5, although another broker said he thought W120/125 was more realistic.

Meanwhile, very large crude carriers from the Middle East continued to be fixed at around W72.5/75 on eastward voyages, with the World Phoenix said done at W73 for 255,000 tonnes to South Korea for Hyundai and the Tokyo Maru at W76 for Yukong.
West Africa/U.S. Gulf VLCCs remained at about W65, while 130,000 tonne vessels dipped to W87.5 from W90 as cargoes were being fixed on the larger ships, brokers said.
Inter-U.K./Cont fuel oil dipped to W240 from W245 for 25,000 tonnes, while in the Med it was steady at W200.
In the western hemisphere, rates were little changed, with 70,000 tonne crude cargoes at W175 and 50,000 tonne fuel oil stems at W190. --Michael Rank, London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
